evidence: Traupman 89: in good time, in plenty of time, mātūrē
terms.comment: Earlier than usual is the comparative mātūrius. Early in the morning is bene māne (see very early); in good time, temperī (see in good time). Gellius records that mātūrē properly meant “at the right moment, neither too soon nor too late” (Gell. 10.11.2).

evidence: Phaedr. 3.19.2: parāre cēnam jussus est mātūrius

phrases.latin: invītat Canius postrīdiē familiārēs suōs, venit ipse mātūrē
phrases.english: the next day Canius invites his friends, and comes early himself

phrases.latin: Aesōpus dominō sōlus cum esset familia, parāre cēnam jussus est mātūrius
phrases.english: Aesop, being his master’s only servant, was told to get dinner ready earlier than usual
